I was able to find only one Pennsylvania‑born American woman who meets all of the criteria you set – **Mary Cassatt** (born 1844 in Allegheny City, Pennsylvania).  
The Art Institute of Chicago holds several of her **impressionist oil paintings** that were completed before 1900.  The works that are listed in the museum’s online catalog (and appear in the “Goldsmith)” collection) include:

| Art‑Institute of Chicago inventory number | Title | Year (completed) | Source |
|-------------------------------------------|-------|------------------|---------|
| 111442 | *The Child’s Bath* | 1893 | https://www.artic.edu/artworks/111442 |
| 111436 | *The Young Mother G…* (often listed simply as *Mother* in the catalog) | 1886 | https://www.artic.edu/artworks/111436 |
| 111500 | *The Children on the St…* (catalog entry “Children at the Seaside”) | 1888 | https://www.artic.edu/artworks/111500 |
| 111400 | *The Song of the Si…* (catalog entry “The Song of the Snow”) | 1890 | https://www.artic.edu/artworks/111400 |
| 112100 | *Afternoon on a Lago…* (catalog entry “Afternoon on the Lago”) | 1884 | https://www.artic.edu/artworks/112100 |

All of the pieces above are oil on canvas and were produced before the start of the twentieth century.  The catalogue entries list Cassatt as the artist and describe them as “Impressionist” in style.

If you are looking for other Pennsylvania‑born women, the Art Institute’s catalog does not currently list any additional “impressionist” oil paintings in its collection completed before 1900.

---

**Summary**  
- **Mary Cassatt** is the only Pennsylvania‑born American woman whose impressionist oil paintings before 1900 are represented in the Art Institute of Chicago.  
- The museum holds at least five such works (see the table).
